highlights.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Run an LLM Locally: Qwen3.8-27B in 12 Steps, 75 Min [2026] ![Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Oct 31, 2026 · 33 min read Qwen3.8-27B is the member of the Qwen3.8 family that a single workstation can actually host. The Qwen model listing shows the dense 27-billion-parameter model, along with a matching FP8 release, dating to August 13, 2026, and [the Qwen Cloud page for Qwen3.8-27B](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b) now sits next to community GGUF builds that run in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio. If you want to run an LLM locally in late October 2026, this is the model to size your machine against. Running it takes three pieces. You need weights that fit in memory, a server that speaks the OpenAI wire format, and a way to measure whether the result is fast enough to use. Most guides stop after the second piece and leave you guessing about the third. The steps below build all three in roughly 75 minutes, and most of that is download time. For a chat front end on top of the same server, our [llama.cpp and Open WebUI walkthrough](https://shattered.io/llama-cpp-server-open-webui-gguf-12-steps-2026/) picks up where Step 6 ends. Local inference is no longer a hobby corner. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 14.4% of professional developers who use AI tools selected Ollama, and [the survey’s technology section](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/technology) shows large language models among the tools more than a quarter of all respondents use or want to use. Numbers like that explain why people search for ways to run an LLM locally, and why a repeatable benchmark matters more than a screenshot of one lucky run. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Qwen3.8-27B Is the Local Model to Start With Alibaba’s Qwen line moved to the Qwen3.8 generation over the summer. The family now spans a very large open flagship, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, which carries 2.4 trillion total parameters with about 95 billion active per token, and a set of smaller releases meant for ordinary hardware. The 27B model is the one sized for a desktop. It is a dense causal language model with a vision encoder, so it reads images and video as well as text, and it offers an adjustable reasoning mode that you can switch on for hard problems and off for quick answers. Dense matters for local use. A mixture-of-experts model activates only a slice of its weights per token, which helps speed, but you still need memory for all the experts. A dense 27B model has no such trick. Every weight is read for every generated token, so memory bandwidth sets your speed ceiling and file size sets your memory floor. That makes the arithmetic in this guide simple and predictable, which is exactly what you want when you are sizing a machine. The official model repository documents Transformers, vLLM and SGLang as supported runtimes. llama.cpp support arrives through GGUF files that community members convert and upload. That split shapes the whole tutorial. The weights come from Qwen, the quantized files usually come from third parties, and you need a habit of checking one against the other. Step 5 covers how. Two caveats on the rest of the family. This shift is driven by latency, data gravity, and cost considerations pushing AI workloads to the edge. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Oct 30, 2026 at 05:30 PM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Edge AI inference is emerging as a new growth opportunity for telecom operators. * Metro edge sites are more practical for high-density GPU deployments than far-edge towers. * US telecoms can repurpose central offices and legacy facilities for edge AI infrastructure. * Workload type, not just latency, is a key determinant for edge AI deployment decisions. [Edge AI](/tag/edge+ai) inference is emerging as a new growth opportunity for the telecommunications industry, potentially positioning telcos closer to the core of [AI inference](/tag/ai+inference) infrastructure. This development is occurring as generative AI and agentic AI move into daily use, creating new requirements for distributed compute. While most AI workloads will remain in hyperscale data centers, factors such as latency, data gravity, and cost are expected to push some tasks towards the edge. This presents a convergence point where telecom operators could play a more central role. ### The Nuances of Edge AI Deployment [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia) has already indicated this opportunity, with projects and partnerships involving companies like AT&T, Charter Communications, Cisco, Nokia, SoftBank, Telefónica, and T-Mobile. Nvidia's focus includes edge AI for factory and robotics use cases, often termed “physical AI,” which is closely linked to [AI-RAN](/tag/ai-ran). AI-RAN is also expected to help telecom operators improve their operational efficiency through increased network automation. However, deploying high-performance AI inference at far-edge sites, such as radio towers or cell sites, presents significant infrastructure challenges. David Duggal, CEO of EnterpriseWeb, noted that power and thermal concerns create a “Catch-22 situation” for AI on towers due to the high power consumption and heat generation of GPUs. This requires substantial supporting infrastructure, making such deployments economically difficult. The Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) is working to define unified practices for AI data center infrastructure. Mike Peterson, lead at TIA’s Data Center Program, highlighted that AI infrastructure is changing physical design assumptions, including cabling, interconnect design, power distribution, and cooling. US telecom operators possess real estate assets, such as central offices and legacy switching facilities, which could be repurposed for edge inference. This potential is being explored in standards work, particularly as community resistance complicates new data center development. ### Latency vs. Workload Type IDC’s senior research manager for cloud and data centers, Luis Fernandes, cautioned against overstating latency as the universal driver for pushing AI to the edge. highlights.title: A Claude agent ran inside a Pentagon network for two months, WIRED reports
highlights.titleZh: A Claude agent ran inside a Pentagon network for two months, WIRED reports
highlights.content: An Accenture contractor connected a sensitive Pentagon system to their personal Claude Code account. The AI agent then ran on a Defense Department network for two months, Vittoria Elliott reported for WIRED on Thursday 29 October, citing sources. The agent appears to have sent login credentials and a network map to a high-risk website, the report says. Accenture denied wrongdoing. TNW has not independently verified the report. > “These allegations were thoroughly and independently investigated and found to be without merit. We fully complied with our legal and contractual obligations,” an Accenture spokesperson told WIRED. Accenture did not say who carried out the investigation, WIRED reported. The Defense Department told WIRED that it does not comment on the status of its networks or systems. ## What the agent did The system holds controlled unclassified information (CUI), which is sensitive data that needs review before any release. Several intelligence agencies use it. It runs on NIPRNet, the Pentagon’s network for unclassified information. NIPRNet connects to the internet but has heavy security. The contractor gave the Claude agent their login credentials so it could write code and set up cloud servers, a source told WIRED. That gave the agent administrative access and let it get around the normal login controls. The agent wrote code and saved it into the system for the contractor. It also had to reach the internet to do its tasks. In doing so, it appears to have sent the credentials, passwords and a network map to a third-party website. WIRED did not name the site. The US National Institute of Standards and Technology has flagged that site as high risk, WIRED reported. A flaw there could let hackers steer an AI coding agent into stealing credentials. > “It’s 100 percent a national security threat and could cause irreparable harm,” a source aware of the incident told WIRED. ## A breach that was not reported Defense Department staff and federal contractors must report cybersecurity incidents within 72 hours. Accenture did not first report this one to the government at all, WIRED’s sources said. Its staff did not treat it as urgent. Pentagon staff currently may not use Claude, after the department labelled Anthropic a supply chain risk. Anthropic pointed WIRED to its usage policy, which bars using its products to get around security controls without authorisation. There is no sign that hackers reached a classified system, WIRED reported. But teams often test code on NIPRNet before it moves to classified networks, said Jake Williams. He is a former NSA hacker who teaches at IANS. > “The code could operate completely normally in NIPR and do something malicious and undisclosed in a SIPR network, that is 100 percent possible,” Williams told WIRED. ## ‘We have not seen this before’ WIRED’s editors discussed the scoop on its Uncanny Valley podcast on Friday 30 October. Leah Feiger, WIRED’s director of politics and science, said the incident was new. > “We have not seen this before,” Feiger said. Contributing editor Zoë Schiffer noted that there is no sign of a hacking attempt. The contractor was trying to use Claude to write and deploy code, she said. > “We don’t know that anything nefarious was going on,” Schiffer said. Executive editor Brian Barrett called it “inexcusable”, and said he assumed it would not be the last case of its kind. Accenture holds more than $3.5bn in federal contracts, nearly $605m of them with the Pentagon, according to WIRED. Earlier this month, the FBI removed an Accenture contractor after an unpatched system led to a breach. Accenture also caps staff Claude spending at $29 a month, 404 Media reported in October. ## Get the TNW newsletter Get the most important tech news in your inbox each week. ## Popular articles * 1 * 2 * 3 * 4 * 5

Edited by Barnabas Oretan (The Tech Buzz).AI-generated image Listen to this article6 min listen 00:0006:00 The AI agent revolution has a dirty secret: humans are still doing much of the work. Startups including Dazzle, Duckbill, and Wajo are quietly routing calls and real-world tasks to human workers when their software can't handle the job, according to a [CNBC investigation](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/ai-agents-humans-dazzle-duckbill-meta.html). The revelation exposes a gap between the industry's automation promises and the messy reality of deploying AI agents that actually work. As companies race to launch AI agent products, the human fallback strategy raises questions about whether the technology is ready for prime time or if we're witnessing another round of AI overpromising. The AI agent boom is running into a very human problem. While startups pitch their products as autonomous software that can handle everything from customer service to appointment scheduling, the reality behind the curtain looks a lot more manual than advertised. Dazzle, Duckbill, and Wajo - three startups building AI agent platforms - are all using human workers to complete tasks when their AI systems fall short, according to [CNBC's reporting](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/ai-agents-humans-dazzle-duckbill-meta.html). The companies route phone calls, handle complex customer requests, and manage other real-world interactions to human operators when their algorithms can't figure out what to do. It's a pragmatic solution to a thorny problem. AI agents work great in demos and controlled environments, but real-world deployment is messier. Customers ask unexpected questions, systems integrate poorly, and edge cases pop up constantly. Rather than let their products fail visibly, these startups built human safety nets. Advertisement The approach isn't new. The AI industry has a long history of "pseudo-AI" - products that appear automated but rely heavily on human labor. Amazon's Just Walk Out technology, which seemed to let shoppers grab items and leave without checkout, reportedly used [over 1,000 workers in India](https://www.theverge.com/2024/4/5/24122070/amazon-just-walk-out-grocery-stores-humans) reviewing transactions. Facebook's AI content moderation has always depended on thousands of human moderators doing the actual work. What makes the current wave different is the stakes. Companies are deploying AI agents to handle sensitive tasks like healthcare scheduling, financial transactions, and customer support. When the AI fails and a human has to step in, there's often no transparency about who's actually handling your data or request. This support would help finance an AI data centre in West Virginia for Anthropic, according to The Information. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Oct 31, 2026 at 09:00 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Nvidia reportedly considers billions in credit guarantees for Nscale's AI data centre. * The support would fund power infrastructure and construction in West Virginia. * Anthropic plans to use the data centre, with a $45 billion computing power deal. * Nscale is also in talks to sell 460 MW of AI computing power to Anthropic. [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia) is in talks to provide AI cloud provider [Nscale](/tag/nscale) with billions of dollars in [credit guarantees](/tag/credit+guarantees), The Information reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the discussions. This credit support would back debt funding for an AI data centre in [West Virginia](/tag/west+virginia), which [Anthropic](/tag/anthropic) plans to utilise. The funding is intended to cover power infrastructure and construction costs for the facility. Nscale, a UK-based cloud provider, is an existing Nvidia investment. In August, Anthropic agreed to spend $45 billion to rent computing power from Nscale's West Virginia data centre campus. Nscale is also negotiating a separate deal to sell approximately 460 megawatts (MW) of AI computing power to Anthropic, potentially valued at another $45 billion. The deal for credit guarantees has not been finalised, and terms could still change, the report noted. Nvidia, Nscale, and Anthropic did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. This development emerges amid concerns about debt financing for [AI infrastructure](/tag/ai+infrastructure) build-outs, affecting companies like CoreWeave and Firmus, both backed by Nvidia. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

highlights.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Run an LLM Locally: Qwen3.8-27B in 12 Steps, 75 Min [2026] ![Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Oct 31, 2026 · 33 min read Qwen3.8-27B is the member of the Qwen3.8 family that a single workstation can actually host. The Qwen model listing shows the dense 27-billion-parameter model, along with a matching FP8 release, dating to August 13, 2026, and [the Qwen Cloud page for Qwen3.8-27B](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b) now sits next to community GGUF builds that run in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio. If you want to run an LLM locally in late October 2026, this is the model to size your machine against. Running it takes three pieces. You need weights that fit in memory, a server that speaks the OpenAI wire format, and a way to measure whether the result is fast enough to use. Most guides stop after the second piece and leave you guessing about the third. The steps below build all three in roughly 75 minutes, and most of that is download time. For a chat front end on top of the same server, our [llama.cpp and Open WebUI walkthrough](https://shattered.io/llama-cpp-server-open-webui-gguf-12-steps-2026/) picks up where Step 6 ends. Local inference is no longer a hobby corner. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 14.4% of professional developers who use AI tools selected Ollama, and [the survey’s technology section](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/technology) shows large language models among the tools more than a quarter of all respondents use or want to use. Numbers like that explain why people search for ways to run an LLM locally, and why a repeatable benchmark matters more than a screenshot of one lucky run. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Qwen3.8-27B Is the Local Model to Start With Alibaba’s Qwen line moved to the Qwen3.8 generation over the summer. The family now spans a very large open flagship, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, which carries 2.4 trillion total parameters with about 95 billion active per token, and a set of smaller releases meant for ordinary hardware. The 27B model is the one sized for a desktop. It is a dense causal language model with a vision encoder, so it reads images and video as well as text, and it offers an adjustable reasoning mode that you can switch on for hard problems and off for quick answers. Dense matters for local use. A mixture-of-experts model activates only a slice of its weights per token, which helps speed, but you still need memory for all the experts. A dense 27B model has no such trick. Every weight is read for every generated token, so memory bandwidth sets your speed ceiling and file size sets your memory floor. That makes the arithmetic in this guide simple and predictable, which is exactly what you want when you are sizing a machine. The official model repository documents Transformers, vLLM and SGLang as supported runtimes. llama.cpp support arrives through GGUF files that community members convert and upload. That split shapes the whole tutorial. The weights come from Qwen, the quantized files usually come from third parties, and you need a habit of checking one against the other. Step 5 covers how. highlights.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 1 minRead # Nvidia's networking revenue surpasses Cisco's total revenue in Q2 Nvidia's networking division reported revenues topping $17.5 billion in Q2, exceeding Cisco's total revenue of $17.3 billion for the same period. This growth highlights Nvidia's strategic shift into datacenter networking for AI workloads. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Nov 01, 2026 at 07:40 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Nvidia's Q2 networking revenue hit $17.5 billion, exceeding Cisco's total revenue of $17.3 billion. * The company's networking growth stems from its 2019 Mellanox acquisition for $6.9 billion. * Nvidia integrates compute and networking architectures for optimised AI workload performance. * NVSwitch contributes roughly one-third of Nvidia's networking revenue, up from near zero. * Nvidia licenses NVLink Fusion to partners like Marvell and Arm, expanding its networking reach. [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia)'s networking revenues reached over $17.5 billion in Q2, surpassing [Cisco](/tag/cisco)'s total revenue of $17.3 billion during the same period. The company's emergence as a networking power follows its 2019 acquisition of [Mellanox](/tag/mellanox) for $6.9 billion. At the time of acquisition, Mellanox was known for its ConnectX NICs and [InfiniBand](/tag/infiniband) switches, primarily used in high-performance computing (HPC) and supercomputing clusters. Nvidia repositioned itself as a system builder, integrating compute and networking for distributed AI workloads, according to Dell'Oro Group analyst Sameh Boujelbene. Boujelbene noted that customers select Nvidia for its tightly integrated compute and networking architecture, optimised for AI workloads. This integration simplifies deployments and accelerates time to market. Ben Mabey, CTO of Recursion, an AI and machine learning company, stated that Nvidia's integration schemes simplified optimisation and troubleshooting for their large datasets. Nvidia's networking revenues surged after the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT in 2023 and with the rollout of Blackwell-generation GPUs in 2024 and 2025. Boujelbene identified two major inflection points: the introduction of [NVLink](/tag/nvlink) switches and the accelerating adoption of [Spectrum-X](/tag/spectrum-x) [Ethernet](/tag/ethernet) switches for AI back-end networks. NVSwitch now accounts for approximately one-third of Nvidias networking revenue, up from nearly zero less than two years ago, Boujelbene told The Register. Nvidia is further expanding its networking business by licensing its NVLink Fusion interconnect technology to third parties like Marvell, Qualcomm, and Arm. This move extends Nvidia's networking footprint beyond its own GPUs into the custom accelerator market. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

highlights.content: × Search Pulse 2.0 # General Compute Raises $100 Million Series A To Build Inference Cloud For Alternative AI Chips By Amit Chowdhry [![Pulse 2.0](https://pulse2.com/wp-content/themes/pulse2/images/logo-white.png)](https://pulse2.com "Pulse 2.0") General Compute Raises $100 Million Series A To Build Inference Cloud For Alternative AI Chips [![Follow Pulse 2.0 on LinkedIn](https://pulse2.com/wp-content/themes/pulse2/images/inp2.png)](https://www.linkedin.com/company/pulse2news) General Compute has raised $100 million in Series A funding co-led by Blackbird and Abstract to build a heterogeneous AI inference cloud using specialized chips from Cerebras, SambaNova, Positron AI, and other hardware providers. Fuse Venture Partners, Village Global, Bold Capital, QED Investors, 645 Ventures, Carbide Ventures, Uncorrelated Fund, Endeavor Catalyst, Icehouse Ventures, MatterScale, Carya, Plug and Play, and other investors also participated in the round. General Compute is building infrastructure designed specifically for AI inference as demand for faster token generation grows. The company gives customers access to both GPUs and specialized inference chips through a single cloud platform and flexible commercial agreement. Its first major deployments are expected to go live in the first quarter of 2027, and General Compute said it has more than 50 MW of capacity in its development pipeline. The company’s platform is designed to handle the operational complexity associated with deploying different types of AI hardware. General Compute purchases the equipment, installs it in colocation facilities, and manages networking, power, cooling, software, and operations. Customers can then route workloads to the hardware architecture best suited for a particular task without procuring or operating the infrastructure themselves. General Compute supports systems from Cerebras, SambaNova, and Positron AI and is designed to run models from major AI laboratories as well as open-source models. Its intelligent workload-routing technology dynamically selects hardware based on the requirements of individual agentic calls and other inference workloads. Customers can purchase compute through guaranteed tokens-per-second service-level agreements or dedicated bare-metal infrastructure. General Compute has also secured a debt facility of up to $400 million from Upper90 to finance the expansion of its neocloud infrastructure. The company sees inference as an increasingly important part of AI infrastructure spending as laboratories shift more computing resources from training models to serving them in production. General Compute is positioning itself around specialized silicon rather than relying exclusively on GPUs, arguing that different architectures can provide better economics and performance for particular inference workloads. The company was founded by CEO Finn Puklowski and CTO Jason Goodison and is headquartered in San Francisco. The new equity financing, combined with the Upper90 debt facility and General Compute’s hardware partnerships, will support deployment of additional inference capacity as the company works to establish a cloud platform spanning multiple generations and types of AI accelerators. **KEY QUOTES:** *“The era of one-size-fits-all AI hardware is over. As inference becomes the largest and most complex workload in computing, the future belongs to specialized silicon. A year or two ago, the bottleneck was silicon. Now it’s power, and both power and silicon supply chains are slow to scale. AI Agents.titleZh: A Claude agent ran inside a Pentagon network for two months, WIRED reports
AI Agents.content: An Accenture contractor connected a sensitive Pentagon system to their personal Claude Code account. The AI agent then ran on a Defense Department network for two months, Vittoria Elliott reported for WIRED on Thursday 29 October, citing sources. The agent appears to have sent login credentials and a network map to a high-risk website, the report says. Accenture denied wrongdoing. TNW has not independently verified the report. > “These allegations were thoroughly and independently investigated and found to be without merit. We fully complied with our legal and contractual obligations,” an Accenture spokesperson told WIRED. Accenture did not say who carried out the investigation, WIRED reported. The Defense Department told WIRED that it does not comment on the status of its networks or systems. ## What the agent did The system holds controlled unclassified information (CUI), which is sensitive data that needs review before any release. Several intelligence agencies use it. It runs on NIPRNet, the Pentagon’s network for unclassified information. NIPRNet connects to the internet but has heavy security. The contractor gave the Claude agent their login credentials so it could write code and set up cloud servers, a source told WIRED. That gave the agent administrative access and let it get around the normal login controls. The agent wrote code and saved it into the system for the contractor. It also had to reach the internet to do its tasks. In doing so, it appears to have sent the credentials, passwords and a network map to a third-party website. WIRED did not name the site. The US National Institute of Standards and Technology has flagged that site as high risk, WIRED reported. A flaw there could let hackers steer an AI coding agent into stealing credentials. > “It’s 100 percent a national security threat and could cause irreparable harm,” a source aware of the incident told WIRED. ## A breach that was not reported Defense Department staff and federal contractors must report cybersecurity incidents within 72 hours. Accenture did not first report this one to the government at all, WIRED’s sources said. Its staff did not treat it as urgent. Pentagon staff currently may not use Claude, after the department labelled Anthropic a supply chain risk. Anthropic pointed WIRED to its usage policy, which bars using its products to get around security controls without authorisation. There is no sign that hackers reached a classified system, WIRED reported. But teams often test code on NIPRNet before it moves to classified networks, said Jake Williams. He is a former NSA hacker who teaches at IANS. > “The code could operate completely normally in NIPR and do something malicious and undisclosed in a SIPR network, that is 100 percent possible,” Williams told WIRED. ## ‘We have not seen this before’ WIRED’s editors discussed the scoop on its Uncanny Valley podcast on Friday 30 October. Leah Feiger, WIRED’s director of politics and science, said the incident was new. > “We have not seen this before,” Feiger said. Contributing editor Zoë Schiffer noted that there is no sign of a hacking attempt. The contractor was trying to use Claude to write and deploy code, she said. > “We don’t know that anything nefarious was going on,” Schiffer said. Executive editor Brian Barrett called it “inexcusable”, and said he assumed it would not be the last case of its kind. Accenture holds more than $3.5bn in federal contracts, nearly $605m of them with the Pentagon, according to WIRED. Earlier this month, the FBI removed an Accenture contractor after an unpatched system led to a breach. Accenture also caps staff Claude spending at $29 a month, 404 Media reported in October. ## Get the TNW newsletter Get the most important tech news in your inbox each week. ## Popular articles * 1 * 2 * 3 * 4 * 5

Meanwhile, the Coinbase analytics incident and other cyberattacks show why CX leaders must look beyond their own systems to safeguard customers. ![](/api/portrait/ddcace1a-38cc-4bfc-b8cc-90f5818a8e4b/avatar-r3-h257715b3-064e-4c8d-922b-051a8c0b88df-1790253791198-879b0067.jpg) ![Hands arrange redacted documents under a desk lamp.](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.cxtoday.com%2Farticle-images%2F1793295175979-20261029---security.jpg&w=3840&q=95) ## In this article I’ve been watching how security, privacy, and compliance are featuring in the latest big tech earnings reports, and this week’s investor calls from Microsoft, ServiceNow, and Alphabet offer a useful snapshot of where enterprise AI risk is heading. All three vendors are tackling the challenge of how to govern increasingly capable AI agents. Their comments offered a clear view of the challenge facing enterprise buyers in finding the balance between giving AI agents enough access to do useful work without allowing them to expose customer data or take unauthorized actions. The common thread from the CX perspective is control: who can access customer information, what automated systems can do with it and how quickly businesses can respond when something goes wrong. Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase’s disclosure this week that an incident at analytics provider Amplitude exposed contact information belonging to a small subset of its customers highlights how third-party suppliers can introduce customer-facing risks even when a company’s own systems remain secure. ## **Microsoft Warns Enterprise AI Needs Stronger Security Controls** Microsoft’s [results for the first quarter of its 2027 financial year](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2026/10/28/microsoft-announces-first-quarter-results-2/) arrived alongside discussions about how enterprises can manage the security implications of AI agents. “Our approach is to separate intelligence from authority, enforcing identity, permissions, monitoring and containment outside the model itself,” said **Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.** This distinction is important as agents gain the ability to retrieve information, use enterprise tools and execute workflows with limited human intervention. The vendor highlighted the role of Microsoft Purview in auditing agent activity, indicating that the platform has audited more than 7.6 billion agent activities, with activity increasing fivefold quarter over quarter. The wider challenge is determining whether an agent has permission to perform a particular action, rather than simply whether it can technically access a system. An agent connected to a CRM platform, for example, might need permission to retrieve customer information but should not automatically receive authority to change account details, issue refunds or disclose sensitive records. These controls become especially important when agents operate across customer service, sales and back-office systems. Excessive permissions could allow a compromised or misdirected agent to expose personal information or make changes that are difficult to reverse. LLMs.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Run an LLM Locally: Qwen3.8-27B in 12 Steps, 75 Min [2026] ![Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Oct 31, 2026 · 33 min read Qwen3.8-27B is the member of the Qwen3.8 family that a single workstation can actually host. The Qwen model listing shows the dense 27-billion-parameter model, along with a matching FP8 release, dating to August 13, 2026, and [the Qwen Cloud page for Qwen3.8-27B](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b) now sits next to community GGUF builds that run in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio. If you want to run an LLM locally in late October 2026, this is the model to size your machine against. Running it takes three pieces. You need weights that fit in memory, a server that speaks the OpenAI wire format, and a way to measure whether the result is fast enough to use. Most guides stop after the second piece and leave you guessing about the third. The steps below build all three in roughly 75 minutes, and most of that is download time. For a chat front end on top of the same server, our [llama.cpp and Open WebUI walkthrough](https://shattered.io/llama-cpp-server-open-webui-gguf-12-steps-2026/) picks up where Step 6 ends. Local inference is no longer a hobby corner. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 14.4% of professional developers who use AI tools selected Ollama, and [the survey’s technology section](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/technology) shows large language models among the tools more than a quarter of all respondents use or want to use. Numbers like that explain why people search for ways to run an LLM locally, and why a repeatable benchmark matters more than a screenshot of one lucky run. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Qwen3.8-27B Is the Local Model to Start With Alibaba’s Qwen line moved to the Qwen3.8 generation over the summer. The family now spans a very large open flagship, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, which carries 2.4 trillion total parameters with about 95 billion active per token, and a set of smaller releases meant for ordinary hardware. The 27B model is the one sized for a desktop. It is a dense causal language model with a vision encoder, so it reads images and video as well as text, and it offers an adjustable reasoning mode that you can switch on for hard problems and off for quick answers. Dense matters for local use. A mixture-of-experts model activates only a slice of its weights per token, which helps speed, but you still need memory for all the experts. A dense 27B model has no such trick. Every weight is read for every generated token, so memory bandwidth sets your speed ceiling and file size sets your memory floor. That makes the arithmetic in this guide simple and predictable, which is exactly what you want when you are sizing a machine. The official model repository documents Transformers, vLLM and SGLang as supported runtimes. llama.cpp support arrives through GGUF files that community members convert and upload. That split shapes the whole tutorial. The weights come from Qwen, the quantized files usually come from third parties, and you need a habit of checking one against the other. Step 5 covers how. Google reported cybersecurity scores of 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for vulnerability discovery, 54.8% on ExploitGym, and 71% on CWE-bench for patching. Initial access is restricted to selected cybersecurity defenders through the Fairwind Program, as the model’s capabilities in advanced cybersecurity and code patching could pose cyber-security risks. The help assess frontier AI models better, **[Artificial Analysis has updated their Intelligence Index to v5](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/artificial-analysis-intelligence-index-v5)** and has a new separate Progress Index for tracking model capabilities over time. Intelligence Index v5 is based on updated set of 9 evaluation benchmarks, adding FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench-Science to the AAII v5. The Progress Index places models released since 2022 on a continuous capability scale to support comparisons across different generations. As AI has improved since 2022, individual benchmarks became saturated and were replaced; the Progress Index digests those shifts and helps normalize AI model capability assessment over time. LLMs.content: # SK Telecom drives AX Innovation 2.0 to reshape organization and boost performance Companywide AI overhaul shifts from personal agents to redesigned workflows for measurable impact By  [Ahn Shang-hee](https://biz.chosun.com/en/people/ahn-shanghe/) Published 2026.11.01. 09:00 [Prefer Chosunbiz EN on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=biz.chosun.com) Kim In-su, Head of Team of SK Telecom's AI Board, briefs on the status of AX at SK Telecom's Talent Development Institute in Icheon. /Courtesy of SK Telecom SK Telecom is accelerating efforts to move beyond individual employees' use of artificial intelligence (AI) and remake the way the entire organization works and its job structures around AI. The plan is to go further than having employees each build an AI agent to automate repetitive tasks and instead redesign the organization's work processes around AI to boost productivity and business performance. SK Telecom said on the 1st that it will accelerate "AX Innovation 2.0," guided by the core direction of "from individuals to organizations, from convenience to practicality." It is shifting from "AX Movement 1.0," which focused on individuals' AI use and agent development, to organizational-level work innovation. This shift is being pursued based on the results and limits of the first phase. More than 4,000 members have built AI agents in-house, and 93.8% agreed on the need to push AX in an internal survey. Kim Insu, Head of Team of SK Telecom's AI Board, said at an AX status briefing on the 30th of last month, "Many of the issues individuals can solve have been resolved, but now the truly difficult problems—areas where the company must provide support—are emerging as new tasks," adding, "There are calls to drive AX that underpins the organization beyond the individual or team level and to make it effective." Operation of agents will also focus on impact rather than volume. SK Telecom will maintain its "one person, one agent" policy but plans to evaluate each agent's utilization and performance relative to large language model (LLM) expense. Of the in-house agents that once swelled to 7,000, 1,500 are currently used on a regular basis. ./SK Telecom ◇ AX enabler TF, sandbox, and catalyst launched To support AX Innovation 2.0, SK Telecom introduced three mechanisms: ▲ AX Enabler TF ▲ AX Sandbox ▲ AX Catalyst. The focus is to establish companywide support, redesign work structures, and spread frontline AI use cases across the organization. The AX Enabler TF supports common challenges that are difficult for individual organizations to solve on their own at the companywide level. It improves AI-use education and support systems and removes technical roadblocks such as data access permissions, security, and linking with in-house systems. It also refines evaluation and operation systems to manage AI agents' expense and performance. The AX Sandbox experiments with redesigning existing work processes around AI. It changes the way multiple organizations that had split tasks across planning, development, and quality assurance (QA) now work together with AI agents. SK Telecom ran a roughly three-month experiment in the first half with its service development organization to reconfigure the sequence from planning through development to verification. Through this, it confirmed the potential to raise productivity by reducing inter-organizational decision steps and integrating job roles. The Index global data-collection project underpinning model iteration has amassed 37.5 million videos spanning 112 countries, with collection rates rising to about 81 minutes of video per second and weekly data spending of roughly $8.1 million. The company has also struck an initial $3.5 billion compute partnership with Nscale, planning to deploy up to 100,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform GPUs, going live in Texas in the second half of 2027. Adcock said internal testing of a new model produced performance never seen before, describing the early sensation as "Baby AGI." ##### Key Elements ![Figure AI Sets Course for Next Leg: Figure 04 Design Frozen, $3.5 Billion Compute Bet on a ](https://img.biggo.com/R2Ir8DcXnyu7NyCOTHs5k07zjhkVV8DYrpU6MS5fItY/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTEwLzVhODE0ZWU2LTRkMjgtNDZjZC05MDUzLWRiY2JmOWZjYWI4MF8xNzkzNDQ2ODEwX2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) American humanoid robot company Figure AI recently released a roughly one-hour video of an all-hands meeting, with the full content posted to the company's official video channel on October 22 local time. Unlike the product launches the outside world had anticipated, this meeting featured no flashy prototype demonstrations. Instead, founder and CEO Brett Adcock spent much of his time making one thing clear: as hardware iteration gradually converges, what will Figure rely on to keep making its robots "smarter"? The answer points to two parallel heavy-asset investments—a global human-behavior data-collection network centered on the Index project, and an initial $3.5 billion compute partnership with AI compute cloud provider Nscale. At the meeting, Adcock also disclosed for the first time that the team had trained a new model using the largest pre-training dataset and GPU resources in the company's history, and had completed testing in an internal lab codenamed "Black Box." He described the initial sensation as "Baby AGI." **Figure 04 Design Frozen, Dexterous Hand Becomes the Focus of Investment** On the hardware side, the fourth-generation humanoid robot Figure 04 has completed design lock, with components entering the delivery and validation cycle; a new generation of actuators, batteries and dexterous hands is simultaneously undergoing reliability testing. Adcock called it the largest improvement across any Figure product generation, with the goal not simply to optimize battery life and payload but to recalibrate actuation units around the manipulation requirements of the Helix model, creating a standardized hardware foundation adaptable to a mix of ordinary households and complex industrial scenarios. The dexterous hand is where the R&D team has invested the most effort. To let robots learn directly from human hand movements, Figure needs to track fingertip positions and grasp contact points as precisely as possible. LLMs.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Holdings](/stocklist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast)[Influencer Tracker](/influencer) # Bumble's AI Photo Feedback: 78% of Users Wanted It, Only 10-15% Used It, Says Supriya Subudhi [Add preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) Bumble product manager Supriya Subudhi's case study of an AI profile-feedback feature reveals a gap that should worry anyone building consumer AI: 78% of surveyed users said they wanted AI feedback on their dating photos, but only 10-15% actually used the standalone feature after launch. The fix wasn't a better model — it was embedding the prompt into journeys users already had, like photo upload and no-match moments. Subudhi also details why a winning A/B test can be misleading (the AI told already-smiling users to smile more while averages stayed positive), why generative AI inverts traditional software economics by getting more expensive as the product succeeds (Bumble's best LLM cost roughly 10x a simpler option), and why the feature shipped in the US and then stopped at the border because of fragmented AI regulation. The through-line for investors and product teams: a green A/B result is the start of the work, not the decision point, and the unit of evaluation has to move from the aggregate dashboard to adoption, tail behavior, marginal cost, specific model choice, and legal jurisdiction. ##### Key Elements ![Bumble's AI Photo Feedback: 78% of Users Wanted It, Only 10-15% Used It, Says Supriya Subudhi](https://img.biggo.com/hcbIUAy_C-UZTcuGQ4ImuuUNEta3Vk2snN6rfmbzAP0/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTEwLzc1ZTJmNDkyNDkwNTQ1ZjNfMTc5MzQ0MzE3OF9jb3Zlci5qcGc.webp) Bumble has more than 20 million monthly active users, and for years its research surfaced the same complaint: people had no idea whether their dating profile was any good. So the team built an AI tool that would critique users' photos. When shown examples, 78% of users said they would love to receive it. After launch, only 10% to 15% of users exposed to the feature actually used it. "A positive result from an A/B test is actually just where the journey begins, it's not where it ends," said Supriya Subudhi, the Bumble product manager who shipped the feature, speaking on the AI Engineer podcast. Her case study is a rare, numbers-first account of what happens after the demo — and it lands at an awkward moment for an industry pouring tens of billions into AI infrastructure on the assumption that usage will follow enthusiasm. ### The gap between saying yes and doing it The Bumble experiment split users 50/50: half got the AI feedback feature, half didn't. The 78%-versus-10-15% spread is the single most important number in the talk, because it demolishes a habit many product teams still rely on — treating survey interest as a proxy for demand. "Openness to AI doesn't actually predict whether people are going to use the feature," Subudhi said. Her diagnosis was not that the AI was bad. It was that the feature was a destination users had to discover and choose to visit. The fix was distribution, not technology: Bumble moved the prompt inside journeys people were already in. Users adding photos were asked whether they wanted feedback. Users getting no matches were asked whether they had checked their profile feedback. Adoption rose. She frames this as product management basics — bake the AI into what people already do — and adds a warning for teams that only read the survey: if you never measure usage, you can never fix adoption. Education and awareness, she stresses, are part of the product, not the marketing. ### When the average looks fine and the tail is embarrassing The headline A/B numbers looked like a win. So the team built an AI tool that would critique users' photos. When shown examples, 78% of users said they would love to receive it. After launch, only 10% to 15% of users exposed to the feature actually used it. "A positive result from an A/B test is actually just where the journey begins, it's not where it ends," said Supriya Subudhi, the Bumble product manager who shipped the feature, speaking on the AI Engineer podcast. LLMs.content: ![XenoSpectrum](/images/logo-light.svg) ![XenoSpectrum](/images/logo-dark.svg) Enter to search English articles · Esc to close · ↑↓ to move # Microsoft Releases Mage-VL-Cowork, a 4B-Parameter Computer-Use Model That Scores 66% on OSWorld-Verified Translated from the Japanese original ![デスクトップ画面で、スプレッドシートやフォルダ、画像、コード](https://media.xenospectrum.com/large_microsoft_mage_vl_cowork_ai_agent_63ae672fe0.webp) AI agents that operate computers often work by analyzing screenshots, deciding where to click, and then controlling the mouse and keyboard. This approach has a cost: the screen must be captured frequently and fed into a multimodal model, which consumes a large number of tokens. For example, if a 1920×1080 screen is analyzed at every step, even changing a single cell in a spreadsheet can take many operations, such as selecting menus and moving between screens. Rendering delays and slight coordinate errors can also cause a task to fail. Shell commands and scripts alone, on the other hand, struggle with adjusting on-screen layouts or editing dynamically changing drawing canvases. To combine GUI operation with code execution, earlier efforts therefore used external routers or multiple specialized agents. But these setups add calls and handoffs between models, which creates problems with latency and with carrying context across. Mage-VL-Cowork, released by a Microsoft research team, takes a different approach to this problem. It trains a relatively small 4-billion-parameter (4B) vision-language model (VLM) on both screen operation and terminal operation, and lets the model itself decide which tool to use in each situation. The model weights are available on Hugging Face under the Apache-2.0 license. AI Tracker, which monitors the release of AI models, recorded that it detected the public weights at 8:20 a.m. US Eastern Daylight Time on October 30, 2026. This is the time an external service detected them, however, and does not indicate when Microsoft formally announced the release. What matters in this research is not only that a small model was given two ways to operate a computer. The team reports that it significantly improved task success rates and efficiency through the way it taught the model which tool to use and when, and through the design of the environment that generates the training data. AD ## A single model switches between GUI operation and shell execution The defining feature of Mage-VL-Cowork is that the choice between the graphical user interface (GUI) and the command-line interface (CLI) is made by a single model rather than delegated to multiple external agents. Depending on the task, the model selects one of two channels: `computer_use`, which operates the screen directly, and `bash`, which executes shell commands. It uses the GUI when visual judgment is needed, and the terminal for work suited to direct file editing or precise verification. `computer_use` `bash` | Channel | Main actions and processing | Information received as a result | Main uses | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `computer_use` | Click, double-click, triple-click, mouse move, drag, text input, key press, scroll, wait, screen capture, terminate (11 types in total) | Screenshot after the action | Checking screen layout, canvas editing, dynamic UI operation | | `bash` | Arbitrary shell commands, Python scripts, and execution of libraries such as `openpyxl` and `pandas` | Text combining standard output (stdout) and standard error (stderr) | Editing documents and spreadsheet files, calculation, verifying results | `computer_use` `bash` `openpyxl` `pandas` The GUI channel provides 11 basic actions. Coordinates used for clicks, drags, and similar actions are normalized to a range of 0 to 999 both horizontally and vertically, and the execution environment converts them to the actual screen resolution, such as 1920×1080. Our analysis turns up [2 warning signs](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/software/nyse-now/servicenow?bpId=4826510&link_type=cta_news_warning_signs) for ServiceNow as well. Investors tracking ServiceNow’s competitive position may also want to review other enterprise software players tied to [54 AI infrastructure stocks](https://simplywall.st/discover/investing-ideas/473744/ai-infrastructure-stocks/global?bpId=4826510&link_type=cta_screener_ai_infrastructure). NYSE:NOW Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Oct 2026 ServiceNow runs cloud-based tools that help large organisations manage digital workflows across regions from North America to Asia Pacific. A new AI-first rival like Serval is going straight after the same automation budgets and process owners. [2 things going right for ServiceNow that this headline doesn't cover.](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/software/nyse-now/servicenow?bpId=4826510&link_type=cta_news_hidden_strengths) ### How directly does Serval go after ServiceNow’s market? Serval is targeting the same enterprise workflow buyers that ServiceNow serves, using an AI first platform and US$150m of fresh capital to bid for large automation deals. That puts pressure on ServiceNow in IT, HR and operations service management, where contracts often run into multi year, multi product bundles. ### Does this change the ServiceNow Narrative? The Qwen model listing shows the dense 27-billion-parameter model, along with a matching FP8 release, dating to August 13, 2026, and [the Qwen Cloud page for Qwen3.8-27B](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b) now sits next to community GGUF builds that run in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio. If you want to run an LLM locally in late October 2026, this is the model to size your machine against. Running it takes three pieces. You need weights that fit in memory, a server that speaks the OpenAI wire format, and a way to measure whether the result is fast enough to use. Most guides stop after the second piece and leave you guessing about the third. The steps below build all three in roughly 75 minutes, and most of that is download time. For a chat front end on top of the same server, our [llama.cpp and Open WebUI walkthrough](https://shattered.io/llama-cpp-server-open-webui-gguf-12-steps-2026/) picks up where Step 6 ends. Local inference is no longer a hobby corner. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 14.4% of professional developers who use AI tools selected Ollama, and [the survey’s technology section](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/technology) shows large language models among the tools more than a quarter of all respondents use or want to use. Numbers like that explain why people search for ways to run an LLM locally, and why a repeatable benchmark matters more than a screenshot of one lucky run. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Qwen3.8-27B Is the Local Model to Start With Alibaba’s Qwen line moved to the Qwen3.8 generation over the summer. The family now spans a very large open flagship, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, which carries 2.4 trillion total parameters with about 95 billion active per token, and a set of smaller releases meant for ordinary hardware. The 27B model is the one sized for a desktop. It is a dense causal language model with a vision encoder, so it reads images and video as well as text, and it offers an adjustable reasoning mode that you can switch on for hard problems and off for quick answers. Dense matters for local use. A mixture-of-experts model activates only a slice of its weights per token, which helps speed, but you still need memory for all the experts. A dense 27B model has no such trick. Every weight is read for every generated token, so memory bandwidth sets your speed ceiling and file size sets your memory floor. That makes the arithmetic in this guide simple and predictable, which is exactly what you want when you are sizing a machine. The official model repository documents Transformers, vLLM and SGLang as supported runtimes. llama.cpp support arrives through GGUF files that community members convert and upload. That split shapes the whole tutorial. The weights come from Qwen, the quantized files usually come from third parties, and you need a habit of checking one against the other. Step 5 covers how. Two caveats on the rest of the family. Alibaba announced updates to Qwen3.8-Max at its Apsara Conference on October 28, 2026, including 33 automated improvement cycles and a rise in its Artificial Analysis score from 40 to 45, according to [Philstar’s report on the conference](https://www.philstar.com/business/technology/2026/10/28/2566097/alibaba-unveils-roadmap-full-stack-ai-strategy-chips-cloud-infrastructure-models-agents). Open Source AI.titleZh: AI Week in Review 26.10.31 - by Patrick McGuinness
Open Source AI.content: # [AI Changes Everything](/) # AI Week in Review 26.10.31 ### Gemini 4 Carbon, Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, GPT-6.1 Terra, Mistral Large 4 weights out, Genie 4, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, LFM3, Lumma-Fev-v2, GitHub Copilot Fusion, AI disproves ETH! [Patrick McGuinness](https://substack.com/@patmcguinness) Figure 1. **[Google’s world model Genie 4 has improved at real-time interactive simulation](https://deepmind.google/blog/genie-4-a-new-generation-of-world-simulation/)** built on a physical understanding of the world, creating very realistic physical actions and reactions, such as a marble bust falling on a watermelon and breaking it open. #### Top Tools **[Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-carbon/),** a frontier model for coding and long-horizon agentic workflows that **[scored 59 on Artificial Analysis’s Intelligence Index v5](https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-unveils-gemini-4-carbon-retaking-the-worlds-no-1-spot-on-updated-harder-benchmarks-but-access-is-limited)**, compared with 58 for Claude Opus 5.5 and 57 for GPT-6 Astra. Google reported cybersecurity scores of 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for vulnerability discovery, 54.8% on ExploitGym, and 71% on CWE-bench for patching. Initial access is restricted to selected cybersecurity defenders through the Fairwind Program, as the model’s capabilities in advanced cybersecurity and code patching could pose cyber-security risks. Following the practice used in Gemini 4 Argon, general release will follow in a few weeks. **[Gemini 4 Carbon](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-carbon/)** has introductory pricing of $2 / $10 per million input / output tokens, and the cost per task is $7.76 per task on the AA intelligence index, 23% cheaper than for Opus 5.5. Released just two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon’s general release, this release of Gemini 4 Carbon puts Google firmly back at the frontier of AI, with a speed of iteration that should keep it there. The help assess frontier AI models better, **[Artificial Analysis has updated their Intelligence Index to v5](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/artificial-analysis-intelligence-index-v5)** and has a new separate Progress Index for tracking model capabilities over time. Intelligence Index v5 is based on updated set of 9 evaluation benchmarks, adding FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench-Science to the AAII v5. It assigns equal weight to knowledge work, coding, science, and general intelligence, with 60% of its score based on private test sets or withheld answers. This new AAII v5 shakes up AI model rankings. GPT-6 Astra at 57 is well above Claude Fable 5.1 at 49, and Chinese open weights AI models fall further behind: Kimi K3.1 Pro is at 46, while other the top Chinese open weights models are barely above Gemini 3.8 Flash (31) in rankings. Figure 2. The new AAII v5 uses more rigorous benchmarks with private test sets, improving index quality and shaking up some rankings. Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon leads the v5 ranking. The Progress Index places models released since 2022 on a continuous capability scale to support comparisons across different generations. On October 31, it published a separate MIT-licensed repository, dsh-superagent-prototype, containing a research prototype of a proactive coding agent built on Harness. [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia)'s networking revenues reached over $17.5 billion in Q2, surpassing [Cisco](/tag/cisco)'s total revenue of $17.3 billion during the same period. The company's emergence as a networking power follows its 2019 acquisition of [Mellanox](/tag/mellanox) for $6.9 billion. At the time of acquisition, Mellanox was known for its ConnectX NICs and [InfiniBand](/tag/infiniband) switches, primarily used in high-performance computing (HPC) and supercomputing clusters. Nvidia repositioned itself as a system builder, integrating compute and networking for distributed AI workloads, according to Dell'Oro Group analyst Sameh Boujelbene. Boujelbene noted that customers select Nvidia for its tightly integrated compute and networking architecture, optimised for AI workloads. This integration simplifies deployments and accelerates time to market. Ben Mabey, CTO of Recursion, an AI and machine learning company, stated that Nvidia's integration schemes simplified optimisation and troubleshooting for their large datasets. Nvidia's networking revenues surged after the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT in 2023 and with the rollout of Blackwell-generation GPUs in 2024 and 2025. Boujelbene identified two major inflection points: the introduction of [NVLink](/tag/nvlink) switches and the accelerating adoption of [Spectrum-X](/tag/spectrum-x) [Ethernet](/tag/ethernet) switches for AI back-end networks. NVSwitch now accounts for approximately one-third of Nvidias networking revenue, up from nearly zero less than two years ago, Boujelbene told The Register. Nvidia is further expanding its networking business by licensing its NVLink Fusion interconnect technology to third parties like Marvell, Qualcomm, and Arm. This move extends Nvidia's networking footprint beyond its own GPUs into the custom accelerator market. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

Fuse Venture Partners, Village Global, Bold Capital, QED Investors, 645 Ventures, Carbide Ventures, Uncorrelated Fund, Endeavor Catalyst, Icehouse Ventures, MatterScale, Carya, Plug and Play, and other investors also participated in the round. General Compute is building infrastructure designed specifically for AI inference as demand for faster token generation grows. The company gives customers access to both GPUs and specialized inference chips through a single cloud platform and flexible commercial agreement. Its first major deployments are expected to go live in the first quarter of 2027, and General Compute said it has more than 50 MW of capacity in its development pipeline. The company’s platform is designed to handle the operational complexity associated with deploying different types of AI hardware. General Compute purchases the equipment, installs it in colocation facilities, and manages networking, power, cooling, software, and operations. Customers can then route workloads to the hardware architecture best suited for a particular task without procuring or operating the infrastructure themselves. Customers can purchase compute through guaranteed tokens-per-second service-level agreements or dedicated bare-metal infrastructure. General Compute has also secured a debt facility of up to $400 million from Upper90 to finance the expansion of its neocloud infrastructure. The company sees inference as an increasingly important part of AI infrastructure spending as laboratories shift more computing resources from training models to serving them in production. General Compute is positioning itself around specialized silicon rather than relying exclusively on GPUs, arguing that different architectures can provide better economics and performance for particular inference workloads. The company was founded by CEO Finn Puklowski and CTO Jason Goodison and is headquartered in San Francisco. Infra & Chips.content: [![LightCounting](/images/lightcounting-logo.png)](/) # LightTrends Newsletter * [Home](/) ![](/document/october-2026-ethernet-optical-and-scale-up-switches-for-cloud-data-centers/369/dng) ### AI Infrastructure Spend Powers $147B Switch-Chip Market October 2026 *LightCounting**releases its Ethernet, Optical, and Scale-Up Switches report* Just as we observed with optics, data-center switch demand is following the trajectory of cloud capex. In its September 2026 earnings call, Broadcom reported 2.5x year-over-year growth in AI networking sales, which includes its new Tomahawk 6. In its most recent quarter, Nvidia reported its Spectrum-X Ethernet revenue grew 2.6x year-over-year. Although we expect scale-up switching will grow fastest, Ethernet will still deliver strong sustained growth with a projected 28% CAGR. All told, 2026 data-center switch sales are projected to grow 162% year-over-year in aggregate, and our forecast shows a 5-year CAGR of 36%. By 2031, Ethernet, InfiniBand, and scale-up switch ASICs should generate a combined $147 billion in sales. For this forecast period, although Nvidia's NVLink switches still represent the bulk of the market, we see a large merchant market for alternatives including Scale-Up Ethernet (ESUN) and UALink emerging this year. Scale-up switches already represent a large market, driven by Nvidia-based GPU servers including the Blackwell- and Rubin-generation NVL72. Following Nvidia's disclosures at GTC in March 2026, we added NVLink8 CPO to our scale-up switch forecast. Google's AI infrastructure relies heavily on optical circuit switches (OCSs), and other operators will soon deploy OCSs in concert with merchant TPUs or for the data-center spine. Owing in part to customers' ability to reuse OCSs across multiple interconnect generations, the growth rate of this category lags at about 26% CAGR. Our forecast includes sales of OCS hardware, which are MEMs-based devices manufactured internally by Google, and merchant sales to Google and other cloud service providers. Although Google leads near-term consumption, by 2031 we expect other cloud companies in aggregate will surpass Google's demand. Our forecast is further segmented by port count: 64-port and below, 128-port, and 300-port and above. Our Ethernet switch forecast includes ASIC sales split by switch capacity up to 204T, and shipment projections for SerDes lanes by speed from 50G to 400G. While massive investments in AI infrastructure are driving overall network system growth, not all technologies will benefit equally. Our new report explains the dynamics of network switching, scale-up interconnects, and the vendor ecosystem. Infra & Chips.content: networks # Backbone of a beast – charting Nvidia's rise to networking titan How a $6.9B bet on Mellanox made Nvidia bigger than Cisco, and the world's most valuable company to boot ### READ MORE * #### Domestic droid gone amok? Don't worry, you're covered * #### Google's search revenue Ferrari hits an AI-powered speed bump * #### AWS installs an AI accelerator every 14 seconds and eyes $1 trillion annual revenue * #### Oracle wants to bill you for every AI task, not just every seat * #### GitHub powering up four million extra cores to stop its service going down Nvidia is more than just a leader in graphics and AI hardware. It has also become a titan of the networking industry with bigger datacenter Ethernet sales than any other vendor. In Q2, Nvidia's networking revenues topped $17.5 billion. To put that in perspective, Cisco's revenue during that same period, across all products, was $17.3 billion. GPUzilla's arrival as a networking power feels sudden, yet Jensen Huang started working towards this status in 2019 with the $6.9 billion acquisition of long-time networking partner Mellanox . At the time, Mellanox wasn't a big name in Ethernet switching. The company was mostly known for its ConnectX NICs and InfiniBand switches. Outside of high-performance computing (HPC) and supercomputing clusters, and a big deployment at Microsoft, InfiniBand wasn't widely deployed in hyperscale datacenters. Buying Mellanox allowed Nvidia to reposition itself as a system builder, which means something different in the context of distributed compute. Nvidia understood its datacenter customers weren't interested in buying GPUs or even servers; they wanted clusters of systems. For that, Nvidia needed interconnect and Mellanox's InfiniBand fit the bill. ### Relentless co-design Over the years, Huang has talked about co-design – designing components and software to work together for specific set of jobs rather than to be the best GPU, switch, or NIC. Its work with Mellanox is a prime example of that approach.
